questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The theatre culture (relevant to my studies) and the language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Regarding the exchange, quite dificult. The amount of bureuacracy makes the beginning of the exchange experience very confusing and exhausting.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved some help from the Incoming Office at my recieving institution and from my Erasmus Coordinator.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was easy enough to find it, but harder to get out of it. I cannot recommend this particular housing to anyone.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's very nice to live off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was all in all quite confusing, but you just have to hope everything will be okay.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always ask the incoming office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get into all the classes I wanted, but I ended up being very satisfied with the classes I did get.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Participate in the orientation meetings. There is a lot of information, you don't need, but the relevant stuff they tell you is VERY important and helpful in the registration process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was very variyng; some courses where at a highly academic, all most master level and some more first-semester level. The courses particular for Eramus students had a quite low level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A much bigger part for the lessons where made up by student presentations. Otherwise it was quite similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Rituelle Aufführungsformen, Staging Gender, Musik als soziale Utopie und Praxis, Berliner Theater der 1920'er Jahre, Kultur und Politik der Weimarer Republik, Theaterkritik, Tanz und Mode.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: They were all really interesting. Some of them demanded a very high german level and were therefore difficult, but if your German is good enough, I would definitely recommend Theaterkritik, which has a much more practical aspect. I also really liked Rituelle Aufführungsformen, which was the most theoretical of my courses,

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not know you had to pay a Semester Fee and stuff like that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent was all in all more expensive than I expected - the student housing was quite cheap, but also horrible (among other things there were bed bugs in my room) so I had to move out as fast as possible, and rent in Berlin in general is more expensive; also I moved around a lot, so I payed double rent for some months.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They offer a lot of sportcourses (I took a Salsa course) and there's the Collegium Musicum with  two choires, a big band and a symphonic orchestra.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you like to sing, the choir is an amazing opportunity to make friends and be a part of something so nice. Also the dance course was so much fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: THEATRE, museums, music ...

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy enough

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Again, joining the choir really helped me make local friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any big challenges regarded cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cultural appetite for and interest in art

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Check out the non-academic activities!
2. Make sure to go to campus once in a while, also if classes are online - it's really nice place with lots of good libraries etc.. Like a 'student village' just outside the city
3. Take the Vorkurs! It's a good way to start off the exchange; learning some german and meeting some people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find your own place to live! It's hard, but not impossible, and at least my experience with the student housing was very bad.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The whole thing, but to pick just one I have to say the friends I got. I already miss them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Starting off my exchange with bed bugs

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
